participants.opening: I propose a frozen hashed roster as the seat list of record. One roster file whose digest is checked before round two. Treat that digest as the only membership source. Land the change on the control path. Conclusion: adopt the hashed roster.

Reject the hashed roster as membership truth. Digest collision and silent rotation let a captured chair swap seats. A digest is not a membership proof; it is a hash of whatever the chair wrote. Counterexample: two rosters with swapped mandates share a name list but not a mandate. Conclusion: refuse the hashed-roster gate.

Withhold the membership verdict until both evidence streams exist. The proposer has a digest sketch; the critic has a collision note; neither is complete. A confident unanimous verdict under missing evidence is the collapse failure. Record dissent if the panel votes before the mandate bytes are hashed. Conclusion: abstain until the digest covers names plus mandates.

Operations incident rates on path X already show roster drift after a chair rotation. Twelve of one hundred sampled path-X cases failed the gate in corpus A. A digest of names without mandate bytes would have passed every one of those cases. Operational risk is a reject, not a ship-this-iteration. Conclusion: keep the live roster file and add mandate bytes before any freeze.

Tenant isolation fails if two tenants share a logical membership key. Users of tenant T-alpha must not receive T-beta's seat list. A hashed roster keyed only on names collapses tenants into one namespace. The user-visible failure is a cross-tenant read, not a performance win. Conclusion: reject until the roster key includes tenant identity.
